dedupe_keys.name: land id us parcel and land mapping platform with infrastructure layers for data centre siting

description: Land id is a US web and mobile mapping platform for land and property, with parcel boundaries and ownership data for properties nationwide, AI-assisted search, measurement and mapping tools and shareable interactive maps. Its data centre use-case page presents it for finding and scoping sites: users overlay transmission lines, substations, fibre optic routes, water features, land use and contour lines, among more than 40 data layers that also include flood zones and soils, on parcel maps with owner details, then measure parcels, outline buildable areas and draft site plans to share with stakeholders. The company pitches it as an alternative to general GIS software and separate property data subscriptions. Coverage: the United States. Format and access: commercial subscription with a 7-day free trial, in a browser and mobile apps. Caveats: proprietary; the provenance and currency of the infrastructure layers are not documented on the page read, and fibre routes in particular are often approximate. Simulation uses: screening candidate data centre sites for grid and fibre proximity and flood exposure, and building parcel-level exposure layers for infrastructure studies. Related records: the ZEG REST tool is a comparable siting service, and the HIFLD and IM3 data give open transmission and data centre layers.
